spec.description: Clips captured from broadcasts, by clip id, by broadcaster or by category. Exactly one of `id`, `broadcaster_id` and `game_id` is given. A walk over clips reaches roughly a thousand rows before Twitch stops paging; narrow it with `started_at` and `ended_at` windows to go further.

request.title: GetClipsRequest
request.description: Which clips, and which page of them.

broadcaster_id.description: The broadcaster whose clips to get. Mutually exclusive with `game_id` and `id`.

game_id.description: The category whose clips to get. Mutually exclusive with `broadcaster_id` and `id`.

id.description: Clip ids to get, such as `AwkwardHelplessSalamanderSwiftRage`. Sent as repeated `id` query parameters; at most 100. Mutually exclusive with `broadcaster_id` and `game_id`.

started_at.description: Only clips created at or after this instant. Sent as RFC 3339.

ended_at.description: Only clips created at or before this instant. Sent as RFC 3339. Defaults to a week after `started_at`.

is_featured.description: Only featured clips when true, only unfeatured ones when false. Omit for both.

first.description: Rows per page. Range [1, 100]; defaults to 20.

after.description: Cursor for the next page, taken from `pagination.cursor` of the previous response; omit for the first page.

before.description: Cursor for the previous page, taken from `pagination.cursor` of the previous response. The generated walk only pages forward, with `after`.

response.title: ClipsFrame
response.description: The wire frame: one page of clips, and the cursor for the next.

data.description: The clips on this page: most viewed first by broadcaster or category, in the order asked for by id.

id.description: An ID that identifies the clip.

url.description: A URL to the clip on twitch.tv.

embed_url.description: A URL to embed the clip in an iframe.

broadcaster_id.description: The ID of the broadcaster the clip was taken from.

creator_id.description: The ID of the user that made the clip.

video_id.description: The video the clip came from; an empty string where that video is not available.

game_id.description: The category being streamed when the clip was made.

language.description: The language the broadcaster streams in, as an ISO 639-1 two-letter code, or `other`.

view_count.description: How many times the clip has been watched.

thumbnail_url.description: A URL to a thumbnail image of the clip.

duration.description: How long the clip runs, in seconds, to a tenth of a second.

vod_offset.description: How far into the video the clip starts, in seconds; null while the video does not exist yet, which lasts minutes after a clip is made during a live broadcast.

pagination.description: The cursor for the next page. Twitch sends this object empty once there are no more pages.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: Helix authenticates every call, and the machine this spec was written on holds no Twitch application credentials. The Record workflow fills this in: it reads the application client id and secret from the repository secrets TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, mints an app access token through the core, replays this endpoint's `examples/*.request.json` with `truewire capture`, and opens a pull request with the response the API sent.

notes: The response schema is the wire frame, `{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`, and no `envelope.payload` is declared, so the method returns the frame and the rows are `result["data"]` (ADR 0010, authoring rule 6). Unwrapping `data` would put the pagination cursor out of reach: pagination paths resolve inside whatever the method returns, and Helix puts the cursor beside `data`, not inside it. One rule for every Helix method is worth more than unwrapping the five endpoints here that never page.

Twitch ends a walk by sending `pagination` as an *empty object*, not by omitting it and not with a null cursor, so the terminator is `absent_cursor` on `pagination.cursor` and a walk stops on the first page whose `pagination` holds no `cursor`.

Written from the Helix reference at the `docs` URL above. Fields the reference marks deprecated are not declared; an undeclared field passes validation and is dropped from the validated value, so a recording that carries one is still valid. The first recording confirms or corrects the rest.
